Checks for real tool calls and absence of imitation patterns.

eli5.text: The system now has a new end-to-end test that verifies a specific agent correctly resumes work from a previously summarized conversation. This test uses a complex, realistic scenario where part of a coding task (like adding a helper function and running tests) was summarized mid-conversation, and the agent must continue without restarting or copying the summary's format. It checks that the agent makes real tool calls (like editing files) and avoids mimicking the text style of the summary itself. This is a testing improvement behind the scenes; it doesn't change what the agent does for users today, but helps catch regressions in how the agent handles resumed conversations.

ai.title: Simplify context summary format
ai.summary: Context pruner summaries drop 'Previously' prefixes and consolidate user headers to '[USER]'. Reduces token overhead in pruned conversation context. Affects `agents/context-pruner.ts` and related tests.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs out of space to remember a long conversation and needs to summarize what happened earlier, it now writes shorter, cleaner notes. Lines that used to start with 'Previously' now just describe the action directly (for example, 'inspected files' instead of 'Previously inspected files'), and each note about something you asked is labeled simply '[USER]'. The result is a more compact summary that takes up less room in the conversation, leaving more space for the actual discussion. You won't see this summary yourself unless you dig into technical logs; it only changes how the assistant internally tracks what was done earlier in the chat.

ai.title: CLI release 1.0.668 ships OAuth polling, summary, and status bar fixes
ai.summary: The CLI package was bumped to 1.0.668 in `cli/release/package.json` with no code-level changes in this commit, serving as a release marker for the OAuth login polling, context summary continuation, and status bar updates that landed since 1.0.667. This version aggregates the refactor of CLI OAuth login polling to dedicated database queries (migrations 0048/0049 adding `cli_auth_hash` and `hasCliSessionForAuthHash`), the context pruner changes wrapping historical messages in memory artifacts with a synthetic continuation prompt, and the removal of the redundant 'Free session' text from `cli/src/components/status-bar.tsx`. The CLI smoke diagnostic that reads `__CODEBUFF_TREE_SITTER_WASM_PATH__` from `globalThis` and the new complex mid-turn summary e2e tests in `base2-free-summary-format.e2e.test.ts` are also included.
ai.evidence: Only `cli/release/package.json` was modified; the single diff hunk changes the version string from `1.0.667` to `1.0.668`. No functional code files were touched in this commit, consistent with the analysis notes describing it as a release-bump.

eli5.text: This release focuses on making CLI login and long conversations more reliable and readable. You can now sign in to the CLI using a smoother OAuth flow that polls a dedicated database lookup instead of slow complex queries, cutting down login flakiness and replaying old sessions, while session expiry checks now safely handle edge cases. When your conversation gets trimmed to stay within limits, the CLI now clearly separates the summary from your live chat by wrapping history in explicit memory blocks and prefixing old tool logs with 'Previously,' so the AI no longer mistakes the recap for new messages and continues from where you actually left off. Finally, the status bar has been cleaned up to show just the model name and remaining time, removing the redundant 'Free session' text that was taking up space.

ai.title: Fix thinker output display in CLI
ai.summary: Agents like thinker return final output via lastMessage rather than streaming. Previous logic suppressed this content if tool blocks existed, hiding the result. The fix checks for streamed text specifically, appending final content only when no text blocks were streamed. This ensures thinker output displays correctly in the CLI.

eli5.text: When the assistant uses a reasoning step (like the 'thinker') during a task, its final written conclusion was getting hidden in the terminal output before it could be seen. The terminal now displays that final conclusion correctly, so you will see the full chain of reasoning instead of just the intermediate steps. The fix affects anyone running the assistant in a terminal who relies on reading these reasoning blocks.

ai.title: Premium session quota and shared rate limits
ai.summary: Introduced shared premium session quotas (5 sessions / 20 hours) for DeepSeek, Kimi, and GLM models, while MiniMax remains unlimited. CLI components (model selector, status bar, waiting room) now display usage counts and quota states based on `rateLimitsByModel` and `rateLimit` payloads. Database migration 0050 and schema updates support the new session tracking logic.

eli5.text: When you open the model picker in the CLI and hover over DeepSeek, Kimi, or GLM, you'll now see a live counter like '3 of 5 sessions used' instead of just the model name. That cap, five paid sessions per 20-hour window, now applies identically across those three models, while MiniMax stays unlimited. The change is live today: the database migration (0050) and backend snapshot query already back the CLI's usage display, so the 'N of M' line updates in real time as the 20-hour window rolls. If you're on a free or pay-as-you-go plan, nothing about your access changed.

ai.summary: Removed the literal string 'Free session ·' from the CLI status bar rendering in `cli/src/components/status-bar.tsx`. This cleanup eliminates redundant labeling when displaying quota and session remaining time. The change affects only the CLI surface.

If you use the assistant in a terminal, you'll see the same quota and time details, just without the redundant "Free session" text taking up space.
